why: The Tirempire Auto Shop is the single-floor Arroyo garage on Valley Street that Desperate Measures uses as its drop-off and where Small Man, Big Mouth goes wrong. The building, workshop workspots, back yard gate and container bay are base-world geometry, and the kept Arroyo community phase already activates the vanilla kids-and-workers crowd there. This proposal restores the shop's own friendly workshop cohort - eight mechanics, two workshop assistants, a worker to talk to and eight customer cars in the bays and lot - so the yard reads as an open autoshop, and deliberately leaves out the heist's Valentino thugs, corpses, delivery van, stolen truck and gig loot. Owner tour 2026-11-27: the broken Quadra and its nearby welding and scanning scene are omitted under the garage-wreck rule.

open_questions: Walk into the Tirempire yard from Valley Street and confirm it reads as a working autoshop: garage open, tire racks and tools in place, no Valentino guards at the door.

Count the shop crew: expect the friendly cohort (eight mechanics, two assistants, one worker to talk to) around the bays plus the vanilla Arcade kids/workers the Arroyo phase spawns; if only two people are there, the whole-community activation is not sticking.
Check the eight friendly cars: they should sit parked in the bays and lot, not across the road, and should not read as quest-locked props belonging to a gig.
Walk behind the gate into the container bay and confirm it is empty: no delivery van, no Valentino thugs, no Kirk or Big Joe bodies, no delivery truck.
Check the yard for gig loot: no weapon or ammo cases, grenades, consumable kits, toolboxes or floating loot tokens behind the DLC dressing.
Confirm the yard gate #arr_12_warehouse_final_gate can be opened on foot or by car (door policy unseal or another way through) and that the container bay is reachable.
Look for Tirempire signage on the building to confirm this yard is the autoshop the wiki calls Tirempire rather than a neighbouring gas station lot.
